canonical_title: Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A single-volume distillation of PKD's roughly 120 short stories, gathering the pieces that seeded his major novels and the films Blade Runner, Total Recall, Minority Report, and The Adjustment Bureau.
page_summary:
Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick condenses a body of short fiction that runs to well over a hundred pieces, most written in the 1950s, into a single representative volume. It is the book to hand someone who wants the shape of Dick's imagination without the five-volume Collected Stories: the precog visions, the simulacra, the small men outmatched by governments and corporations, the moment when reality slips its frame.

The stories collected here are the seedbed of the later work. 'We Can Remember It for You Wholesale' became Total Recall; 'The Minority Report' became Minority Report; 'Adjustment Team' became The Adjustment Bureau; 'The Second Variety' and 'Paycheck' and others fed further adaptations. Reading them together shows how consistently Dick returned to a handful of questions about authenticity, memory, and control, and how many angles he found on each.

For researchers, this entry serves as a compact map of Dick's short fiction and its afterlife in film and television, and as a bridge between the pulp-magazine origins and the philosophical novels of his maturity.
